title: Collection intervals permit both signs of summer beetle timing trends in four English and Scottish samples in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether fortnightly collection records fix the sign of summer community beetle timing trends. We used 261 location-year records at nine English and Scottish sites in 1993-2003 and 2004-2015. Models controlled location and three sampling-design variables. Midpoint trends were -3.24 to -6.84 days per decade. All four sharp fixed-record ranges permit both signs when capture dates can vary within collection intervals. A single common position within all intervals keeps the four negative signs. All midpoint sampling intervals also include zero. Stricter coverage and interval rules leave both signs possible. The result requires correct counts and collection dates. It concerns observed summer catches, not emergence or a causal climate effect. Selected samples, species mixing, trap activity bias, few sites and shared monitoring methods limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and independent arithmetic checks are supplied. Raw and record-level derived data remain external.

display.caption: Fixed-record coefficient bounds under any allowed capture dates and under one common fractional position in all collection intervals. Black points use midpoint dates. Lines are not confidence intervals.
